title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
script:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman just told AI leaders to stop spreading doomsday warnings.
He made the argument at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference in San Francisco.
Feldman claims that focusing on existential risks is drowning out the benefits of AI.
He suggests the industry should prioritize talking about the actual utility of AI.
Feldman believes public concern is distracting from the current capabilities of these systems.
This comes as Cerebras continues to challenge Nvidia with its massive processor chips.
Should leaders ignore existential risks to focus on current AI performance?

editor.one_line: Strong, punchy script, but visual variety is lacking and feels repetitive.
script_fixes: LINE 6: Replace 'massive processor chips' with 'Wafer Scale Engine' for more specificity.
LINE 7: Make the question more provocative, e.g., 'Is the AI industry's obsession with doomsday holding back real progress?'
visual_notes: line 1: The same photo of Andrew Feldman is held for too long across multiple frames.
line 2: The 'TechCrunch Disrupt' text graphic is repeated across two frames without visual change.
line 5: The visual is static text for too long; needs a cut to a different relevant asset.
